title: v4 drafted from parent ledger D022/D024/D025/D026 cluster trigger
body: Three distinct supervisor frictions surfaced in this week's cross-repo dogfood (plan 004 F001+F002 + plan 010 F002 + SpinDine v2 dispatch). Per parent plan 2026-05-11-001 ledger D026, cluster threshold ≥3 reached. v4 sourced directly from those three D-entries + a fourth derivative (supervisor checkpointing is the structural fix that addresses the same orphaned-state class as D025 even when shlex isn't the cause). Drafted while signals are fresh; status: draft for operator review before lock.

title: goal_type:infra (consistent with v1/v2/v3)
body: Same framing as v1/v2/v3 plans — harness substrate, not user-facing feature. Avoids Goal Governance V1 objective_contract requirement at lock time.

title: F004 depends_on F003 because F003 enables clean failure records
body: F003 (shlex-safe) makes parse errors produce structured warnings instead of unhandled exceptions. F004 (checkpoint artifacts) then captures the residual failure modes — env errors, missing schemas, OSError. Ordering matters: if F004 lands first, the checkpoint would record shlex crashes verbatim, but the underlying volley would still die mid-run; F003 first means F004 only triages truly-unexpected failures.

title: Out of scope: tee buffering, iterN cost regression, automated retry-on-crash
body: Three deliberately-deferred concerns. (a) Tee buffering of dispatch logs is operator-side (operators can copy from the bash task output file); not a supervisor-side fix. (b) iterN cost regression (D019 in parent) is a single observation so far — defer to v5 if it clusters with other cost signals. (c) Automated retry-on-shlex-crash is a separate concern; F003+F004 deliver clean failure surfaces, retry policy is its own design conversation.

title: Pre-lock self-review tightened F002 + F003
body: Pre-lock review surfaced two gaps in the initial draft. (1) F002 `is_advisory_only_findings_set([])` was vacuously True for empty findings — would auto-promote any verdict=blocked-with-no-findings to paused_on_environmental, but empty findings can also mean auditor crashed mid-run / format error / network failure. No evidence the blocker IS environmental in that case. Patched F002 to require non-empty findings for advisory-only promotion + added new terminal `blocked_no_findings` that surfaces 'auditor unable to produce findings — operator review required' instead of auto-promoting. Acceptance #4 added. (2) F003 assumed the D025 'No closing quotation' shlex error was in our own shlex.split() calls — but the original D025 reproducer didn't pinpoint the call site. If the in-repo audit doesn't surface it, the error could be in a dependency / Pydantic validator / subprocess parser. Added a BACKSTOP step: top-level try/except ValueError around dispatch_volley's iter loop that writes F004 checkpoint + exits cleanly, catching parse failures from anywhere we don't control. Both patches strengthen the plan without expanding scope. Lock: status:draft → active.

title: F002 close-out: paused_on_environmental == stopped_environmental_blocker (synonym; spec_ambiguity)
body: During F002 dispatch, the implementer discovered that v3 F003 already established `stopped_environmental_blocker` as the canonical terminal status string (circuit_breakers.TERMINAL_STATUS). The plan's `paused_on_environmental` language was descriptive — the actual status emitted to integrate with F003's existing handlers MUST be `stopped_environmental_blocker`. The implementer's code emits the canonical name; the implementation logic is correct. Codex iter1 flagged this as high/correctness (literal mismatch with plan text). CLASSIFICATION: spec_ambiguity — exactly the v3 F003 taxonomy class for terminal-name disputes where both readings (descriptive vs canonical) fit. RESOLUTION: code is correct (canonical name wins to preserve F003 backward compat); plan text reverted to the original `paused_on_environmental` language to preserve locked-AC invariant; this D-entry documents the synonymization. F004 (depends_on:F003) implementers can reference both names interchangeably.

title: F002 close-out: test_coverage findings #1+#2 logged as v4.1 candidates
body: Codex iter1 raised two real test_coverage findings beyond the spec_ambiguity terminal-name issue. (a) The F004 replay fixture (test_verdict_blocked_reconciliation_f002.py:540-586) uses a permissive terminal assertion (`not in {blocked, blocked_no_findings, stopped_environmental_blocker}`) rather than strict `== needs_changes` — the implementer noted that the exact terminal depends on no-progress / diminishing-returns thresholds, but codex wants strict pinning. (b) The Plan 010 F002 fixture is hand-coded rather than replaying the actual saved codex envelope. Both are legitimate quality-of-tests improvements; neither is a correctness defect. Logged as v4.1 candidates for a future cleanup commit. Full sweep 1898 passed — implementation logic is sound.

title: F003 close-out: category=parsing vs schema enum (spec_ambiguity)
body: F003 features.json step 3 says findings should be `severity=advisory category=parsing`. Implementer chose category=correctness because audit.schema.json v1.0 enum is {correctness, security, performance, architecture, style, currency, redaction, test_coverage, documentation} — parsing is NOT a valid value. Schema-locked enum means parsing literal would fail validation downstream. Codex iter1 flagged the deviation as medium/correctness; the deviation is real but forced — the spec text and the schema are mutually inconsistent. CLASSIFICATION: spec_ambiguity per v3 F003 taxonomy. RESOLUTION: code stays at category=correctness (only schema-valid option matching repo convention at audit_writer.py:313 + supervisor.py:2438/2460); features.json step 3 spec wording stands as locked-AC. Adding parsing to the enum is a v4.1 candidate that would require an agent-conventions VERSION bump + subtree sync — out of scope for v4 lock-time correction. Operator close-out via dontpanic close --operator-resolved with reason=spec_ambiguity.

title: F003 close-out: test_coverage rigor logged as v4.1 candidate
body: Codex iter1 + iter0 raised the same test_coverage finding: Plan 004 F002 replay test (test_shlex_safe_command_guard_f003.py:462,500) exercises the post-iter accountability layer (_apply_target_accountability) and the per-command shlex wrapper, but does not drive the full supervisor dispatch_volley terminal path with parse-breaking input. The implementer addressed iter0 by loading the real on-disk envelope rather than fabricated commands — that materially upgraded the test from synthetic to real-fixture. Codex iter1 escalated to demand full-volley termination assertion. This is the same test_coverage rigor pattern logged in D007 (v3 F002 closeout). CLASSIFICATION: already-known — not a regression, not a defect, an upgrade of an existing v4.1 carry. RESOLUTION: deferred to v4.1 cleanup commit alongside D007 strict-terminal-pin and Plan 010 F002 fixture replay. Functional F003 scope (shlex wrappers + backstop + 3 failure-mode tests + signed_off implementer at 1916 tests) is delivered.
